title: How Ryan Hoover launched Product Hunt: build an audience first, find a hole and fill it
summary: Ryan Hoover explains how Product Hunt grew from a simple email list into a community, crediting years of blogging and relationships for the initial 300 subscribers. He covers early growth via press and word of mouth, the hardest parts of running a company (firing, momentum), and his advice to build an audience before you launch.

principles.text: Spot a problem you personally have or observe, then build the thing you want to exist.
principles.quote: My dad’s always said, “Find a hole and fill it.”

principles.text: Build an audience before launching; distribution is the hardest part of any product.
principles.quote: The hardest thing is distribution for any kind of product, and even just getting beta users can be really difficult, but if you have an audience of people who care about what you’re doing, you now immediately have access to people to support you and what you’re building.

principles.text: Years of writing and relationships gave Product Hunt its first 300 subscribers; without some following it wouldn't have worked.
principles.quote: without the prior years of blogging and building relationships with other people, Product Hunt wouldn’t have worked if I didn’t have at least some sort of following.

principles.text: Press only works as acquisition when the outlet's readers match your target audience; otherwise it's vanity.
principles.quote: For most companies, press doesn’t reach their actual target audience and it can be a more vanity metric than a growth strategy.

principles.text: Early growth came from press plus sharing and word of mouth from users and makers sharing their product pages.
principles.quote: Those two vehicles were really how Product Hunt grew in the first year.

principles.text: Prioritize ruthlessly: write down three must-do things each week so lesser tasks don't consume the week.
principles.quote: in the beginning of every week I write down, essentially three things that need to get done that week. If I get nothing else done but these three things, then it’s still a win.
